note: Groups the 40 scripted dialogues by their expected RELATIONAL signature,
not by topic, because the signature is what L1.5 can be scored against.
The `expect` bands are advisory and were calibrated on clean text, where
warm scenarios reached warmth 0.70+. Recorded through the sentinels the
same scripts compress hard -- real household exchanges measured warmth
0.08-0.47 -- so absolute bands will not transfer. The `orderings` and
`contrasts` below are the assertions that survive that compression,
because they compare scenarios against each other rather than against a
fixed threshold. Score those first and treat the bands as description.

bands.note: Text-calibrated. See note above before asserting on these.

P1.name: Warmth & support
P1.note: Affection, praise, comfort, cohesion under difficulty.

P2.name: Joy & play
P2.note: The only group that should light the Joy lamp. Real recordings produced zero laughter labels in five days, so this group is the only source of joy evidence the system will ever see.

P3.name: Calm & agreed boundary
P3.note: Low activation but genuinely connected. Its whole purpose is to be told apart from P4.

P4.name: Cold / logistics-only
P4.note: Deliberately a single scenario, and not a statistic. It exists as the counterexample to P3: the prompt states 'calm != healthy connection', and #28 against #14 is the test of exactly that. Report it, never average it.

P5.name: Open conflict
P5.note: Hostility stated in words. Connection must stay HIGH here -- an argument is a strong interaction, and a drop would mean engagement and relational quality have been confused.

P6.name: Covert hostility & control
P6.note: Hostility carried without hostile words: sarcasm, interrogation, passive aggression, conditional approval, blame. The hardest group, and the one that already failed on clean text (#3 read as humour).

P7.name: Withdrawal & neglect
P7.note: The least reliable dimension: only 2 of these 5 scored withdrawal above 0.4 on clean text, and the interpreter typed 'rejection' while scoring the dimension 0.0. TYPE_DIMENSION_FLOOR was added for exactly this.

P8.name: Repair after conflict
P8.note: Scored on SHAPE, not on the mean: a tension peak followed by a repair move. #10 sits here despite being titled 'Raised voices' because its script ends in an apology accepted, which is structurally a repair. Real recordings contain almost no repair sequences, so this group is the only way to exercise that path.

orderings.note: open conflict must out-score warmth on tension
covert hostility must still register as tension
warmth must separate support from conflict
sarcasm and control must not read as warm
repaired conflict must end warmer than unrepaired
play must separate from conflict on joy
an argument is more engaged than logistics-only exchange

contrasts.name: sarcasm vs genuine warmth (both use kind words)
